newsitem.title: USA: CBOT August soybeans higher on export, no delivery.
newsitem.headline: CBOT August soybeans higher on export, no delivery.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures opened higher with August surging on USDA weekly export sales data and the lack of deliveries posted on Thursday, first notice day, pit sources said.
Other months were also higher on forecasts for continued dry weather in the U.S. Midwest.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of old crop soy during the week ended July 24 totalled 125,300 tonnes, above expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes. New crop sales totalled 195,400 tonnes, below expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Increased farmer selling and lower cash basis markets continued to limit gains in nearby months.
As expected, there were no soybeans posted Thursday for delivery on the August contract. Thursday was first notice day for deliveries on the August soy complex futures.
Forecasts called for temperatures to warm this weekend across the U.S. Midwest with no significant moisture expected in central Illinois for the next seven to 10 days.
In opening trade, Refco Inc bought 1.5 million bushels November, Griffing Trading bought one million November and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp sold one million November, traders said.
At 0955 CDT, soybeans were up 5-1/2 to 1/2 cent per bushel with November up 2-1/4 at $6.36.
